title: CFPB money conversation and budgeting tools
supports: Set aside a calm hour to compare take-home income, debts, recurring obligations, caregiving, and what each person wants to keep separate. Agree on how shared bills will be divided and when you will review the arrangement. Keep a record both people can access. A shared budget does not require shared passwords or surrendering control of personal money; safety matters if a partner is controlling.
limitation: Practical steps and time estimates are editorial suggestions; cited facts have the scope stated in the entry.

title: New York Courts divorce FAQs — New York example only
supports: Inventory assets, debts, retirement accounts, and parenting arrangements before agreeing to a settlement. Use your state court self-help service and seek legal advice about disputed property or children. New York, for example, describes equitable distribution rather than an automatic equal split; another state may use different rules. Mediation may help willing parties, but abuse or coercion can make it inappropriate.
limitation: Practical steps and time estimates are editorial suggestions; cited facts have the scope stated in the entry.

title: CFPB family lending and borrowing
supports: Before transferring money, agree on the amount, purpose, repayment schedule if any, and what happens if circumstances change. Write down the agreement and give both people a copy. Consider whether you can afford never to get the money back. For a large or interest-free arrangement, ask a qualified adviser about tax and legal consequences instead of treating a text message as a complete contract.
limitation: Practical steps and time estimates are editorial suggestions; cited facts have the scope stated in the entry.

title: HHS safety planning for an abusive relationship
supports: If you face immediate danger, call 911 when you can safely do so. Otherwise, use a safer device to contact the National Domestic Violence Hotline at 800-799-7233 and plan around your circumstances. Think through a safe destination, transportation, children, medication, and important documents. Leaving can increase danger; an advocate can help plan the timing. Do not announce a departure plan to a person who may retaliate.
limitation: Eligibility and applicability are limited as stated in the entry.

title: USAGov child support services
supports: Contact your state or tribal child support agency to ask about establishing parentage, obtaining an order, collecting support, or reviewing an existing amount. Keep payment records and copies of orders. If your income changes, ask about the formal modification process rather than assuming payments change automatically. Agencies can help pursue support; the government does not simply pay the other parent’s obligation for them.
limitation: Eligibility and applicability are limited as stated in the entry.

title: USAGov child care assistance and Head Start
supports: Ask each provider for its full price, hours, closure calendar, late fees, and licensing information. Then check state child care assistance and your local Head Start program before assuming the posted price is what you must pay. Eligibility, provider participation, and openings differ. Include the time and cost of backup care in your comparison, especially if missed shifts could threaten your job.
limitation: Practical steps and time estimates are editorial suggestions; cited facts have the scope stated in the entry.

title: CDC early intervention and referral routes
supports: Write down concrete examples of the skills or behavior that concern you and discuss them with your child’s clinician. For a child under three, contact the state early intervention program directly; a doctor’s referral is not required. For preschool children three or older, contact the local public school or district special education office. Eligibility comes from evaluation and program rules, not a parent’s ability to buy private therapy.
limitation: Eligibility and applicability are limited as stated in the entry.

title: USAGov school and summer meal programs
supports: Ask your child’s school about breakfast and lunch programs, how eligibility is determined, and whether an application is needed. You can ask during the school year if circumstances change. Before summer, look for local meal sites and applicable summer grocery benefits. Availability and enrollment processes differ by program and location; do not assume a benefit continues automatically when school closes.
limitation: Eligibility and applicability are limited as stated in the entry.

title: CDC drowning prevention
supports: Choose one sober adult to supervise closely without a phone, then explicitly hand off that role if they need a break. Swimming lessons and lifeguards do not remove the need for supervision. Use appropriate life jackets around natural water, restrict unsupervised access to pools, and learn CPR. Inflatable toys are not safety equipment, and water risk also includes bathtubs and unfamiliar homes.
limitation: Eligibility and applicability are limited as stated in the entry.

title: SEC introduction to 529 plans
supports: After protecting current essentials, compare your state’s 529 plan with lower-cost alternatives and read the offering documents. Check eligible expenses, withdrawal restrictions, investment risk, and any state tax incentive. A 529 is an account, not a guaranteed return. Choose investments that fit when the money will be spent and avoid committing money you may need for rent or emergency expenses.
limitation: Practical steps and time estimates are editorial suggestions; cited facts have the scope stated in the entry.

title: Medicare enrollment timing and existing coverage
supports: Most people first become eligible around 65; the usual initial window includes the three months before the birthday month, that month, and the following three months. Confirm your exact dates with Medicare. If you have employer coverage, ask how employer size and current employment affect enrollment. COBRA and retiree coverage are not interchangeable with coverage from current employment. Coordinate HSA contributions before Medicare begins.
limitation: Eligibility and applicability are limited as stated in the entry.

title: SSA retirement planning
supports: Review your earnings record and estimated retirement benefits in your Social Security account. Eligible workers can generally claim from 62, with a higher monthly benefit for delaying up to 70. Consider health, household income needs, work, and spouse or survivor benefits before choosing. The best date is personal; a headline about the largest monthly payment does not decide the household’s best plan.
limitation: Practical steps and time estimates are editorial suggestions; cited facts have the scope stated in the entry.

title: Medicare long-term care coverage limits
supports: List the help a person needs with bathing, meals, dressing, medication, transportation, and supervision. Medicare generally does not pay for ongoing custodial long-term care. Ask about local aging services, Medicaid eligibility, home-based support, and respite options before a caregiver burns out. A temporary skilled-care benefit is not a promise to pay for indefinite assisted living or help at home.
limitation: Practical steps and time estimates are editorial suggestions; cited facts have the scope stated in the entry.

title: NIH advance-care planning checklist
supports: Discuss medical preferences with a trusted person and complete advance-care documents that meet your state’s requirements. Give accessible copies to that person and your clinicians. Separately arrange valid authority for financial decisions; a health care proxy and a financial power of attorney serve different purposes. Review wills and beneficiary designations with appropriate help after major family changes rather than assuming one document handles everything.
limitation: Practical steps and time estimates are editorial suggestions; cited facts have the scope stated in the entry.

title: FTC Funeral Rule and itemized price requirements
supports: Ask funeral providers for prices and compare the specific services your family wants. Covered providers must give you a General Price List when you inquire in person about arrangements, and provide required price information over the phone. Ask which charges are optional and why any item is required. Bring a trusted person to help take notes; a more expensive package is not a measure of love.
limitation: Practical steps and time estimates are editorial suggestions; cited facts have the scope stated in the entry.

title: SSA comparison of disability programs
supports: SSDI is tied to insured status based on covered earnings; SSI considers limited income and resources as well as age, blindness, or disability. Some people qualify for both. Start with Social Security, keep records of functional limitations and treatment, and save every decision notice. Follow the appeal instructions and deadline on a denial. A diagnosis alone does not establish eligibility for every program.
limitation: Practical steps and time estimates are editorial suggestions; cited facts have the scope stated in the entry.

title: Medicaid home and community-based waivers
supports: Contact Medicaid or the state disability services agency about home and community-based services. Ask which program fits the person’s age and needs, what financial and functional tests apply, whether enrollment is capped, and what alternatives exist while waiting. Some waivers can cover personal care, respite, or other support. Benefits and openings differ; getting Medicaid does not automatically guarantee every home-care service.
limitation: Eligibility and applicability are limited as stated in the entry.

title: Department of Justice overview of disability rights
supports: Describe the barrier and the change that would help: accessible documents, communication support, a usable entrance, or an adjustment to a service. Keep a dated record of requests and responses. Disability rights apply in many settings, but the applicable law differs: housing, air travel, employment, and public services do not all use the same complaint process. Use the relevant agency instead of buying an unofficial disability certificate.
limitation: Practical steps and time estimates are editorial suggestions; cited facts have the scope stated in the entry.

title: SSA ABLE accounts — 2026 edition
supports: An ABLE account can hold money for qualified disability expenses with special tax and benefit treatment. Starting in 2026, the qualifying disability must generally have begun before age 46, alongside the other eligibility requirements. Compare program fees, contribution rules, SSI balance treatment, and possible Medicaid recovery. Keep expense records and get benefits guidance before a large transfer; ABLE protection has conditions and limits.
limitation: Eligibility and applicability are limited as stated in the entry.

title: USAGov disability employment and training routes
supports: Contact your state vocational rehabilitation agency or a local Center for Independent Living about training and support. If you receive Social Security disability benefits, ask about Ticket to Work and individualized benefits counseling before changing work hours. Report earnings as required and save confirmation. Support programs can help, but each person’s cash benefits and health coverage may respond differently to earnings.
limitation: Eligibility and applicability are limited as stated in the entry.

title: USDA nutrition on a budget
supports: Choose two or three realistic meals, check what is already at home, and make a shopping list around overlapping ingredients. Compare fresh, frozen, and canned options that fit your needs and storage. Build in a quick fallback meal for exhausted evenings. Buying bulk only helps if you can store and use it; include preparation time and transport rather than judging groceries by sticker price alone.
limitation: Practical steps and time estimates are editorial suggestions; cited facts have the scope stated in the entry.

title: Department of Energy home assessment guide
supports: Review bills across seasons and ask your utility about an energy assessment. Start with the largest practical sources of waste identified for your home. Compare installed cost, maintenance, expected savings, and how long you will stay before buying equipment. Renters should check permission before changes. Confirm current incentives with the administering program; an old webpage or salesperson’s projection is not an approved rebate.

title: USAGov public libraries and available resources
supports: Ask your local public library about digital books, audiobooks, research databases, computer access, learning resources, and community events. Check residency and borrowing rules and try the service before paying for something similar. Collections and waiting lists vary. A library card can also be an entry point to local information and human help when an online form or job search gets confusing.

title: USDA budget resources including unit pricing
supports: Compare equal units, such as price per ounce, and then ask how much you will use before it spoils or becomes clutter. Include membership charges, delivery fees, and the travel required to get a discount. Try a smaller package if you are unsure you like the product. A lower unit price is useful only when the purchase fits your cash flow and real needs.

title: CDC suggestions for improving social connection
supports: Choose a recurring way to see or contact people: a walk, library group, shared meal, community class, or a call with a friend. Make the first commitment small enough to keep. Reach out for help and offer it where you can without exhausting yourself. If cost, illness, transport, or disability is a barrier, look for an accessible alternative rather than treating isolation as a personal failure.
limitation: Eligibility and applicability are limited as stated in the entry.

title: CDC emergency water storage
supports: Store at least one gallon of water per person per day for three days; add more for heat, illness, pregnancy, and pets, and build toward a longer supply if feasible. Keep essential medicines, contact information, chargers, and an evacuation plan accessible. Coordinate assistance for mobility or powered medical equipment. Follow local evacuation instructions; supplies are useful, but they do not make an unsafe location safe.
limitation: Practical steps and time estimates are editorial suggestions; cited facts have the scope stated in the entry.

title: CPSC carbon monoxide prevention
supports: Install CO alarms on every level and outside sleeping areas, with battery backup as appropriate, and follow testing instructions. Never run a generator inside a home or garage, even with doors open; CPSC advises placing it outside at least 20 feet from the home with exhaust directed away. If an alarm sounds or poisoning is suspected, get outside to fresh air and call 911.
limitation: Eligibility and applicability are limited as stated in the entry.

title: State Department international travel checklist
supports: Confirm passport validity, destination entry rules, relevant travel advice, and whether your current insurance pays for care abroad. If a coverage gap matters, compare travel medical and evacuation insurance including exclusions and pre-existing-condition provisions. Keep accessible copies of documents and a trusted contact’s details. U.S. consular assistance is valuable, but the government does not pay your routine medical or unexpected travel bills.
limitation: Eligibility and applicability are limited as stated in the entry.

title: NHTSA seat belt guidance
supports: Buckle up in every seating position, set navigation before departure, and keep the phone out of your hands. Arrange a sober driver or another ride before using substances that impair driving. If tiredness makes you unsafe, stop and rest rather than relying on willpower. A short, familiar drive still requires attention; use a suitable child restraint for children and follow its instructions.

title: CDC firearm injury prevention and secure storage
supports: If firearms are present, store them unloaded and locked, with ammunition secured separately, and keep keys or combinations inaccessible to unauthorized people. Hiding a firearm is not secure storage. Ask about storage where children visit. If someone in the home may harm themselves or others, seek immediate crisis help and arrange safer access restrictions consistent with local law; do not attempt to seize a weapon from someone threatening violence.

supports: Find an accredited Veterans Service Organization representative through VA and ask whether they can help with your claim or decision review. Accredited VSO claim assistance is free; attorneys and claims agents may charge under applicable rules. Keep your own copies of service records, medical evidence, submissions, and decision letters. Be cautious about anyone guaranteeing a rating or demanding broad access to your accounts.

title: VA health care eligibility
supports: Review VA’s eligibility criteria and apply if your service history may qualify. Ask how enrollment, priority group, copayments, and other insurance affect your care. Do not assume that having a private plan disqualifies you, or that every veteran automatically receives every service free. Keep your care team informed about medications and treatment from other systems so records and prescriptions do not become fragmented.

title: VA GI Bill benefits and comparison resources
supports: Use VA’s comparison tools and your Statement of Benefits to check the approved program, remaining entitlement, tuition coverage, and living-cost support. Ask the school’s certifying official for a written estimate and compare graduation, transfer, and job outcomes. Approval for benefits does not guarantee that a school is a good investment or that every fee will be covered. Review consequences before changing programs or withdrawing.
limitation: Practical steps and time estimates are editorial suggestions; cited facts have the scope stated in the entry.

title: VA-backed home loans
supports: Check your Certificate of Eligibility and compare lender offers using the same home price, loan amount, and closing date. Ask about the funding fee and any exemption, interest rate, closing costs, and monthly taxes and insurance. A possible low or zero down payment does not remove the cost of owning a home. Keep repair reserves and compare with renting if your next move may be soon.
limitation: Practical steps and time estimates are editorial suggestions; cited facts have the scope stated in the entry.

title: DOJ servicemember financial and housing rights
supports: When entering active duty or receiving qualifying orders, ask military legal assistance whether the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act applies to existing debts, housing, vehicle leases, or court proceedings. Keep orders and written notices. Eligibility, notice requirements, and timing matter; a protection for one contract does not cancel all obligations. Contact the lender or landlord through a documented process instead of simply stopping payment.
limitation: Practical steps and time estimates are editorial suggestions; cited facts have the scope stated in the entry.

title: CDC food poisoning prevention
supports: Keep raw meat separate from ready-to-eat food, clean hands and preparation surfaces, and use a food thermometer with the recommended temperature for the food. Refrigerate perishables within two hours, or one hour when exposed to temperatures above 90°F. Thaw safely in the refrigerator, cold water, or microwave. Appearance and smell cannot reliably establish safety, and a bargain is not worth eating recalled food.
limitation: Eligibility and applicability are limited as stated in the entry.

title: EPA radon testing and reduction resources
supports: Use EPA guidance to arrange a radon test appropriate to your home and follow the kit instructions. A neighbor’s result does not measure your home. If the result calls for action, obtain qualified mitigation advice and retest after work. Renters can ask the owner about existing results and responsibilities. For a purchase, clarify testing and mitigation in the inspection process before closing.
limitation: Practical steps and time estimates are editorial suggestions; cited facts have the scope stated in the entry.

title: EPA lead in drinking water
supports: Ask your water utility about service lines and testing, especially in older housing. If lead is a concern, follow local sampling guidance and select a filter certified for lead reduction; replace cartridges on schedule. Use cold water for drinking and cooking. Boiling does not remove lead. A general annual water report may not describe the plumbing inside your home, and private wells need their own testing plan.
limitation: Eligibility and applicability are limited as stated in the entry.

title: CDC heat and health planning
supports: Check local heat risk and identify a reliably cool place, including a public cooling center if needed. Move demanding outdoor activity to cooler hours, take breaks, and check on people who live alone. Ask your clinician about a heat plan if you have medical conditions or take medicines that affect heat tolerance. Plan for refrigerated medicines and powered equipment during outages; do not change prescriptions on your own.
limitation: Eligibility and applicability are limited as stated in the entry.

title: AirNow preparation for wildfire smoke
supports: Check AirNow and local instructions before outdoor activity during smoke events. Identify an indoor room where air can be kept cleaner and consider appropriately sized filtration. Reduce indoor smoke and particle sources. People with heart or lung disease, children, and older adults may need extra precautions. A cleaner room does not override an evacuation order, and a hot sealed room creates another hazard if cooling is unavailable.
limitation: Eligibility and applicability are limited as stated in the entry.

title: State Department guidance for study abroad
supports: Ask your home school which credits will transfer, who awards the transcript, what aid can be used, and what happens if the program is canceled. Compare the full cost including housing, flights, local transportation, insurance, and visa fees. Review the destination’s safety guidance and keep emergency contacts. A beautiful program brochure does not establish credit transfer, scholarship eligibility, or a right to work abroad.
limitation: Practical steps and time estimates are editorial suggestions; cited facts have the scope stated in the entry.

title: State Department business travel and work abroad
supports: Check destination-government visa and work rules with the employer or sponsor before travel, including whether remote work is permitted. Get pay, insurance, housing, termination, and return-travel terms in writing. Research local laws and entry requirements; a U.S. passport is not general permission to work in another country. For a complex assignment, get immigration and tax advice that covers both countries.
limitation: Practical steps and time estimates are editorial suggestions; cited facts have the scope stated in the entry.

title: IRS guidance for U.S. citizens abroad
supports: U.S. citizens generally remain subject to U.S. tax rules on worldwide income while abroad. Review filing requirements, foreign tax relief, and any foreign-account reporting obligations with a qualified adviser. Keep income, tax, account, and travel-day records. Do not assume a foreign income exclusion is automatic or that owing no income tax eliminates reporting. State residency and local-country tax rules need separate attention.
limitation: Practical steps and time estimates are editorial suggestions; cited facts have the scope stated in the entry.

title: CDC traveling abroad with medicine
supports: Check the destination and transit countries’ rules before packing prescription or over-the-counter medicines. Ask about controlled medicines, quantity limits, documentation, and permits. Keep medicines in labeled original packaging and arrange an adequate legal supply with your clinician. Carry essential medication where you can access it during travel. A valid U.S. prescription does not guarantee that the same drug is permitted abroad.
limitation: Eligibility and applicability are limited as stated in the entry.

title: State Department crisis response and evacuation limits
supports: Save local emergency numbers, embassy contacts, documents, and a way to reach family without your usual phone. Enroll in appropriate State Department travel alerts through STEP. Follow local instructions and use safe commercial departure options when advised and available. Government evacuation is not guaranteed and usually involves repayment; onward travel from a safe location may remain your responsibility. Include dependents and pets in planning.
limitation: Eligibility and applicability are limited as stated in the entry.

title: Editorial decision method
supports: First handle a real deadline or a threat to safety, housing, essential care, or income. Then choose one repeatable improvement such as reviewing a recurring bill or making a realistic meal plan. Write the next action and when you will do it. Leave the rest of this guide for later. A list of two achievable actions is easier to evaluate than a promise to overhaul your whole life.

title: Editorial decision method
supports: Write the upfront price, recurring charges, maintenance, exit costs, and time required. Add what could go wrong and whether you can absorb it. Use your own assumptions and test a less favorable case. For example, a cheaper apartment may add commuting time and a car expense. Do not collapse health, relationships, and dollars into a fake universal score; decide which tradeoffs matter to your household.
limitation: Practical steps and time estimates are editorial suggestions; cited facts have the scope stated in the entry.

title: Editorial decision method
supports: Choose one friction point such as repeated errands or distracted work. Record the current pattern briefly, try one change for a week, and compare time, stress, and results. Examples include batching errands or silencing nonessential alerts during a short work block. Keep emergency and caregiving communication available. If the change creates more work than it saves, revise or drop it rather than buying a new productivity system.
limitation: Practical steps and time estimates are editorial suggestions; cited facts have the scope stated in the entry.

title: Editorial decision method
supports: Before a course, subscription, side project, or new routine, define what success would look like and when you will reassess. Decide what would make you stop, change approach, or seek help. Separate a modest reversible trial from a major commitment. Money already spent is a record of the past; the next payment should be judged on the likely value from here.
limitation: Practical steps and time estimates are editorial suggestions; cited facts have the scope stated in the entry.

title: Editorial decision method
supports: Keep a secure index of policies, benefit notices, warranties, important contacts, and upcoming renewal or appeal dates. Store sensitive documents in protected storage, not in a public repository or shared checklist. Give an appropriate trusted person a way to locate essential information. Schedule a brief review after a move, job change, birth, separation, or death; revise the system if maintaining it becomes a burden.
limitation: Practical steps and time estimates are editorial suggestions; cited facts have the scope stated in the entry.

title: FDA safe food handling
supports: Cook immediately after thawing in cold water or microwave.
limitation: Safe handling advice does not establish food safety for an individual recalled or contaminated item.

title: NHTSA drowsy driving
supports: Drowsiness threatens safe driving; adequate sleep and avoiding driving when sleepy are preventive steps.
limitation: No quick trick guarantees alertness.

title: NHTSA drug-impaired driving
supports: Alcohol and impairing drugs can make driving unsafe.
limitation: Effects vary by substance and person; verify medication warnings.

title: CFPB Regulation Z 1026.13(b)(1)
supports: Billing-error notice must be received at the disclosed address no later than 60 days after the first periodic statement reflecting the error was transmitted.
limitation: Specific open-end credit billing-error procedure; not a universal dispute right for all payments.

title: Medicare working past65
supports: HSA contribution coordination may need to account for retroactive Medicare coverage.
limitation: Individual Medicare entitlement timing and account circumstances require verification.

title: USAGov report a death
supports: Notification pathways after a death, including agencies and financial services.
limitation: Notification duties depend on the deceased person’s accounts and benefits.

title: FTC debts and deceased relatives
supports: Estate debt and exceptions to relatives generally not personally owing solely by relationship.
limitation: State laws, joint obligations, and estate-administration conduct can change responsibility.

title: CDC all-hazards preparedness guide
supports: Communication, evacuation, medication and medical-equipment planning, including access needs and pets.
limitation: Historical guide, used only for general preparation principles on pages10–18; not for current disease, evacuation or treatment instructions.
